claims.claim: The Apple II launched with a base price of $1,298 for the 4 KB RAM configuration in June 1977.
claims.episode_span: The board-only version listed at five hundred ninety eight dollars for four kilobytes of RAM. The complete system with case, keyboard, and power supply reached twelve hundred ninety eight dollars.
claims.source_title: Apple releases the Apple II - Event - Computing History
claims.supporting_quote: At launch, prices ranged from $1298 with 4 kB of RAM up to $2638 with the maximum 48 kB of RAM.

claims.claim: The board-only Apple II with 4 KB RAM was priced at $598 in the June 1977 price list.
claims.episode_span: The board-only version listed at five hundred ninety eight dollars for four kilobytes of RAM.

claims.claim: The Apple II used a MOS Technology 6502 microprocessor running at 1 MHz.
claims.episode_span: Wozniak started with the MOS Technology 6502 running at one megahertz, a part already proven in other devices and available for modest cost.
claims.source_title: Apple II goes on sale, June 5, 1977 — EDN
claims.supporting_quote: With a base price of $1298, the computers came with a MOS Technology 6502 microprocessor running at 1 MHz, 4 kB of RAM, an audio cassette interface for loading programs and storing data, and the Integer BASIC programming language built into the ROMs.
